rows.name: PROMPT_TOKENS_MAX

cells.Values and default: Integer number of estimated tokens. The script uses the text in bash arithmetic. It must not be smaller than `PROMPT_TOKENS_MIN`. Otherwise the script exits with status 1. Unset: 15000 estimated tokens.
cells.Effect: It is the upper limit of the prompt size when `PROMPT_MODE` is `long`. Each request of `burst-test.sh` (the script that sends a burst of chat completion requests to a server) draws its size at random between `PROMPT_TOKENS_MIN` and `PROMPT_TOKENS_MAX`. The script counts 3 words as 4 tokens. It builds the passage from whole paragraphs. The passage can be larger than the drawn size. `rinzler` rejects a request when the prompt plus `max_tokens` exceeds its total token limit or the context length of the model. The script counts that request as failed. The range check also runs when `PROMPT_MODE` is `short`. The option `-P` or `--prompt-max` overrides the variable.

rows.name: SEED

cells.Values and default: Integer. The script assigns the text to the bash variable `RANDOM`. The script does not check the text. Unset: the script does not seed `RANDOM`.
cells.Effect: `burst-test.sh` (the script that sends a burst of chat completion requests to a server) assigns a non-empty value to the bash variable `RANDOM` before the first random draw. The draws of arrival offsets, `max_tokens` values, prompt sizes and prompt pairs then come from the seeded generator. A later run with the same value and the same options repeats these draws. The option `-S` or `--seed` overrides the variable. `long` mode makes 3 more draws for each request than `short` mode. rows.name: STREAMING

cells.Values and default: `true` or `false`. The script compares the text with `true`. It also passes the text to `jq` as the JSON value of the request field `stream`. Unset: `true`.
cells.Effect: `true` makes `burst-test.sh` (the script that sends a burst of chat completion requests to a server) send streaming requests. The script then checks that each stream ends with `[DONE]` and holds no error frame. `false` sends blocking requests. The option `-b` or `--blocking` sets `false` and overrides the variable. Text that is not JSON, for example `yes`, makes `jq` fail. Each request then fails before the script sends it. The script sends other JSON, for example `1`, as written. It then reads the response as a blocking response.

rows.name: TRACE_DEST_IP

cells.Set by: A developer who wants the trace on another host.
cells.Values and default: Host name or address of an `scp` destination. `tronperf` adds `:` after the text. `tronperf` does not check the text. Unset: `tronperf` does not copy the trace.
cells.Effect: After a capture without errors, `tronperf` (the script that captures a Perfetto trace of one `runtron` run) copies the trace file to that host with `scp -C`. The destination has no path. `scp` then writes the file into the home directory of the remote user. `tronperf` skips the copy when `runtron`, the `perfetto` client or a Perfetto daemon ends with an error. When `scp` fails, `tronperf` exits with the `scp` status. The trace file is `$HOME/runtron.trace`, or the path given with `--output-file`. `perfetto/wrapper` does not read the variable.

notes: All 12 rows came without hints, so every fact comes from my own read of the code at commit 7eddde7895. Unchanged rows: NUM_USERS, WINDOW_MS, PERFETTO_HOME. PERFETTO_BIN_DIR was 1,349 characters and is now 996. To reach the limit I removed these facts: the sentence about bin/ci/test-perfetto-capture.sh (a test fact, already in the PERFETTO_CAPTURE_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION row), the two lists of required programs in 'Values and default' (the Effect cell names the programs that each script starts), the path of the resolver script in 'Read by' (the Effect cell holds it), and the word 'executable'. I also removed the two counts ('and 2 more files', 'two CI workflows'), added the case where PERFETTO_HOME is also unset, and replaced the unclear 'It takes priority' with 'The variable overrides'. PROMPT_TOKENS_MAX and SEED each held a sentence about a source comment (house rule 6). In PROMPT_TOKENS_MAX I replaced it with the behavior that the code shows: rinzler answers with HTTP status 400 when the prompt plus an explicit max_tokens exceeds its total limit or the model context length (src/rinzler/token-limits.cpp:79, src/rinzler.cpp:3177), and curl --fail makes the script count the request as failed. In SEED I replaced it with the fact that the same value and the same options repeat the draws. PAIRING, PROMPT_MODE, PROMPT_TOKENS_MAX, PROMPT_TOKENS_MIN, SEED and STREAMING named burst-test.sh without a definition (house rule 10). I added the clause that the rows API_KEY to MODEL use. PROMPT_TOKENS_MAX and PROMPT_TOKENS_MIN now say how the text is parsed (bash arithmetic). STREAMING: 'That request' had no clear subject, because every request fails with a non-JSON value. VERBOSE: the first Effect sentence was a count of scripts and did not say what the variable changes. TRACE_DEST_IP: only backticks around the program name runtron. Seen outside this chunk and not changed by me: the row MAX_TOKENS_BASE still holds a 'The script header says' sentence. The rows of table 3.1 define burst-test.sh with three different clauses and use two different 'Set by' texts ('The person who runs', 'A developer who runs'). Two facts about tools come from small commands of my own on bash 5.1.16 and jq 1.6, not from the repository scripts: a word such as abc in bash arithmetic ends a 'set -u' script with the error 'unbound variable', and jq rejects a non-JSON --argjson value with exit status 2. The SEED row holds for runs with the same bash version. Insufficient data for different bash versions: I did not compare the RANDOM sequences of two versions.
